The topic 'Simulation (one random move, page ranks)' introduces simulation_loop.

[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday "random" means every outcome equally likely, which is what Math.random() gives; the random move must instead pick page j with the unequal probability p[page][j].
[1] misconception (M) -> CumulativeOffByOne: wrong rule: The cumulative-probability boundary test is inclusive/exclusive interchangeably. Right rule: Add p[page][j] to sum first and then test r < sum; sum is the right endpoint of interval j, so r lands in interval j with probability equal to its length.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CumulativeOffByOne: Applies LT (r drawn once; for each j: add p[page][j] to sum, then test r < sum) unevenly: e.g. testing before adding on some passes, or drawing a new r for each j. (here mixing in: "the cumulative-probability boundary test is inclusive/exclusive interchangeably")

[0] names_the_element (N): An algorithm: generating a random integer from a discrete distribution (row p[page]) by locating a uniform random number in cumulative intervals.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Think of row p[page] as N intervals of (0, 1) whose lengths are the probabilities; a uniform r from Math.random() falls into interval j with probability p[page][j], and the surfer moves to j.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): r = Math.random() is drawn once; sum = 0.0; j goes 0, 1, ...; on each pass sum += p[page][j] and then if (r < sum) set page = j and break, so the first interval whose right end exceeds r wins.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Returns (through page) one integer 0..N-1; at page 4 of tiny.txt sum takes 0.47, 0.49, 0.96, ... and r = .71 gives page 2.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One move changes page from its current value to j (and leaves freq and p unchanged); the locals r, sum and j live only for that move.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Reads exactly one row p[page]; the row must sum to 1, otherwise r can exceed the final sum and no j is chosen.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Each move starts from the page the previous move produced, and the simulation repeats it T times; the next row used is p[new page].
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): The relational test r < sum decides both the chosen page and the early break; < (not <=) matches the half-open interval endpoint tracked by sum.
[3] relation_to_neighbour (R): Math.random() supplies one uniform double in [0, 1) per move; it must be called once before the j loop, not inside it.
[4] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Sampling plan (search the cumulative sums): sum is a gatherer, j a stepper, and page a most-recent holder of the current location; break ends the search as soon as the interval is found.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CumulativeOffByOne: Changing the search (linear to binary) or the order of pages keeps the distribution of outcomes; replacing r < sum with r <= sum changes it only on a zero-probability event; moving Math.random() into the loop breaks it.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use to draw from any non-uniform discrete distribution (one row of probabilities); for uniform choice Math.random() scaled is enough, and for large N a binary search over the cumulative sums is faster.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Add the entry to sum before testing r < sum. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Test placed before sum += p[page][j]: the first test is r < 0.0 (always false) and every page is chosen from the previous interval, shifting probabilities by one page.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Row p[page] must sum to 1. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: Row sum < 1 (e.g. dangling page, NaN): when r exceeds the final sum the loop ends with no break and page is unchanged.
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: break must exit the search once the interval is found. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: break omitted: page is reassigned on every later j, so the surfer always moves to page N-1 (or the last j with r < sum).

wrong: Whether the test is r < s or r <= s, or whether p[i][j] is added before or after the test, the same page is picked. | right: Add p[page][j] to sum and then test r < sum: sum tracks the endpoints of the intervals defined by row p[page], so the loop finds the interval containing r, and r falls into each interval with probability precisely specified by its length.
The next page is chosen by testing the condition r < sum for each candidate page j in turn.
The random move draws r with Math.random() and then finds the interval of row p[page] that contains r.
The simulation repeats the random move T times, each move starting from the page the previous move reached.
Row p[i] is the probability distribution used to choose the next page when the surfer is on page i.
